findings.text: Provides a contiguous table of indirect branch thunks with one entry per general register, generated from the register enumeration and spaced by the architected thunk stride so callers can dispatch through a register specific speculation safe sequence.

Provides alias domain return untraining with two boot selected encodings, one serializing and diverting to the alias return path and the other performing a direct architected return, allowing the kernel to match the active speculative execution mitigation.

The alias safe return path preserves caller continuation by skipping the transient training slot on the stack before returning, and any fall through past the return or past the paired return thunk reaches a faulting operation, with external interrupt handling required to stay consistent if the sequence changes.

Provides the main domain return mitigation set where architected execution resumes at the address held on the stack top while mispredicted speculation is drawn into a faulting call sequence that is preceded by serialization and bounded by halting operations.

Implements return predictor invalidation by executing an overlapping byte pattern that architecturally behaves as a return in one view and as a predictor evicting operation in another, followed by serialization and a backward transfer that reexecutes the return while straight line speculation remains contained.
Offers a single kernel entry for return untraining that is rewritten at boot to invoke either the retbleed or the SRSO implementation according to the detected processor capability.

Tracks per processor call depth for return stack protection by scaling the stored depth and returning immediately while depth remains, otherwise executing a fixed length sequence of nested calls to refill predictor state, adjusting the stack past the pushed addresses, crediting depth and then returning.

Supplies ITS specific and generic return thunks that both perform an architected return followed by a faulting guard, with the generic form conditionally rewritten at boot to a warning path when entry, SRSO or call depth tracking mitigations are configured.

Exports hand tuned 32 bit string and memory primitives for copy, concatenation, bounded concatenation, character search, length, bounded length, bounded byte search, byte scan and substring search, with the 32 bit string unit opting out of compile time fortification so explicit behavior is preserved.

Copy and concatenation routines always return the destination start, copy the terminating null when it is encountered, locate the existing terminator before appending, and for the bounded append form ensure null termination after at most the requested number of source bytes.

Length and search primitives define edge behavior with length excluding the terminator and bounded length capped by the limit, character search including the terminator position, empty memory search returning null for the finding form and the start address for the scanning form, and scanning returning the match address or the first byte past the region.

Substring search returns the address of the first occurrence of the needle in the haystack or null when absent, with empty needle handling that yields the haystack start through the same comparison path.

Provides a copy from user memory that is safe to invoke from non maskable interrupt context by first validating the user range and checking interrupt access permission, then suppressing faults around an instrumented raw copy and reporting the number of bytes not copied.

User memory clearing routines report the originally requested length regardless of outcome, with the checked form validating accessibility before zeroing and the unchecked form assuming the caller already validated.

User accesses that may fault must be paired with exception table recovery that redirects faults to a common exit, with wide word and trailing byte phases handled separately and with supervisor access to user memory enabled only around the actual reference.

Provides an atomic nontemporal copy from user memory that opens a user access window, uses a cache bypassing block path for large lengths when vector capability is present and otherwise uses the generic user copy path, then closes the window and reports the residual length.
The 32 bit user copy fast path is allowed only when source and destination alignment is compatible for large lengths under the Intel optimization, otherwise the generic path must be used.
Holds a mostly read alignment mask in a dedicated structure instance that the Intel user copy path consults to decide whether wide moves are safe.
Exposes a persistent memory cache writeback operation that cleans caches over a caller supplied address range so that stores become durable.

Discovers AMD NUMA topology by scanning PCI configuration for a matching northbridge, reading the node count, iterating up to eight base limit pairs to register present memory ranges, then assigning contiguous identifier blocks sized by the core domain to each parsed node.

NUMA discovery skips disabled or empty entries and already recorded or excess nodes, fails when interleaving is enabled or the map is unsorted, and clamps discovered ranges to the physical memory bounds before registration.

Northbridge probing covers bus zero with a bounded device scan and function pairing expectations across three chipset generations, while node count comes from a shifted nibble plus one and base limit pairs live at strided configuration offsets with enablement, node identifier and interleave fields at fixed bit positions.
Maintains per processor entry area state consisting of a pointer to the mapped exception stack bundle and a mostly read slot index that selects which entry area replica the processor uses.

Entry area slot indices are unique across all possible processors, assigned sequentially when address space randomization is disabled and drawn randomly without collision otherwise, with a no operation variant when the mapping feature is not built.

Installs a single entry area mapping from a virtual address to a physical page with caller supplied protections, adding the global attribute only when the processor supports global pages and the mapping is present, since the area is shared between user and kernel page tables.

Builds the per processor entry area in order by preparing shadow state, mapping the descriptor table, entry stack and task state, then delegating to exception stack and debug store setup, with the page walking helper advancing both virtual and physical pointers one page at a time.

Exception stacks are mapped individually so guard pages remain effective, covering fault, non maskable, debug and machine check stacks in the full variant plus secure virtualization stacks only inside an encrypted guest, while the compact variant maps only a single double fault stack.

Descriptor and task state mappings must respect writability and contiguity rules with read only tables on 64 bit and writable tables on 32 bit due to task gate and task switch writes, with build time checks that the hardware task state does not cross a page boundary, has the expected size and starts at offset zero.

Entry area and mitigation construction rely on fixed layout facts that the hardware task state occupies one hundred four bytes, the safe stack adjustment skips one eight byte slot, the call depth scale uses a five bit shift and the predictor refill uses sixteen iterations.
